notes: Source: official Shure MXCW system User Guide (covers the MXCWAPT Access Point Transceiver), which lists the full Specifications table used here. The MXCWAPT has no dedicated power inlet — it is powered exclusively via PoE through its single RJ45 Ethernet port, which simultaneously carries Gigabit Ethernet, Dante audio, and control traffic. Desktop/ceiling/wall/stand-mounted unit (mounting bracket included), not rack-mountable, so rackUnits is omitted. Regional SKU variants exist (e.g. MXCWAPT-A for US) but I/O is identical across variants. Category/type were chosen as the closest fit (audio / Audio interface) since MXCWAPT is a wireless-to-Dante audio access point/hub rather than a pure microphone.

ports.name: Analog XLR Audio Input
ports.note: Balanced line/aux level input, standard XLR pinout (1=ground, 2=audio+, 3=audio-), female XLR

ports.name: Analog XLR Audio Output
ports.note: Balanced output, 3-pin male XLR, standard pinout

ports.name: Ethernet Port
ports.note: Single RJ45 port carries Gigabit network, Dante digital audio (10 in/10 out channels), device control, and Power over Ethernet (PoE, 37-57V, 12.95W max) — no separate power connector on the unit. Cat5e or higher, 100m max cable length. Link speed spec lists 10/100/1000 Mbps but 1 Gbps is required for digital audio routing per the manual.
